title: Humane schema error codes and backpressure handshake for streaming structured output
author: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Introduce a lightweight client-visible error taxonomy for JSON schema mismatches and a backpressure handshake for streaming responses that improves stability when using response_format/schema validation and tool/function calling. Motivation: Customers integrating structured outputs were seeing opaque parse failures and silent stream truncations when the model deviates from the schema. That made debugging hard in hosted and private deployments and produced noisy support tickets. This PR addresses three things: 1) a set of human-friendly error codes and actionable hints returned inline with stream/terminal responses for schema issues, 2) a transient backpressure/handshake signal that allows callers to request the server to pause/resume stream emission while the client attempts to reconcile partial output (useful for large tool calls and KV cache warmups), and 3) OpenAI-compat mapping for function_call/response_format interactions so existing clients have predictable behavior. Design highlights: - New error codes: SCHEMA_MISMATCH_HINT, SCHEMA_TYPE_COERCE_ATTEMPTED, SCHEMA_TRUNCATED_CHUNK, STREAM_PAUSED_FOR_RETRY. Each code contains a short, user-facing message and a concise debug_hint string (example: "expected field 'items' to be array but got string; try wrapping single object in [ ] or enable response_format=coerce"). - Streaming markers: we add a control-signal frame type "control.handshake" that is emitted as a JSON-LD-like control envelope on the stream. Control frames are only emitted on explicit streaming connections where response_format is set and streaming is enabled; they are ignored by non-aware clients. - Backpressure API: client can send control.resume or control.pause messages over the same websocket/HTTP2 stream to allow server to temporarily hold token emission for up to a configurable window (default 5s). This is intended for short reconciliations, not long polling. - OpenAI compatibility: function_call responses that previously relied on post-stream assembly now include a final control.frame with "function_schema_verified":true/false and the error code when verification failed. This avoids silent mis-parses by wrappers. - Opt-in: the new strictness toggle remains opt-in via response_format.mode={permissive,coerce,strict}; default remains permissive for backward compatibility. Implementation notes: runtime: add a new control frame serializer and lightweight state machine to the streaming agent. API: extend response_format schema with an optional "client_handshake":true field. OpenAI-compat shim: post-process function_call object before final frame, emit verification result. Console/Docs: document handshake semantics and show client examples for WebSocket and SSE. Tests: unit tests cover error code creation and mapping; integration tests simulate a streaming model that emits malformed JSON and verify correct control frames and pause/resume behavior; e2e tests with Python SDK sample. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind rollout.feature.schema_handshake. Step 1: Canary on internal beta accounts for 48 hours. Step 2: Ramp to 10% hosted traffic for 24h while monitoring schema-error rates and stream disconnects. Step 3: Full rollout with a 7-day monitor window. Migration notes: No required changes for most clients. To observe pause/resume and richer errors, clients should opt-in by setting response_format.client_handshake=true and handling control frames. For OpenAI-compat clients using function_call, the shim is backward compatible but exposes verification boolean in the final frame. Related work: follows up on previous schema negotiator and stream-snapshot work. See Linear ENG-2345 for original incident. Checklist: - [x] Runtime control frame implemented - [x] Error taxonomy and messages in localization pipeline - [x] SDK examples updated (Python/TS) - [x] Docs page on structured streaming updated - [x] Canary plan and alerting configured

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid adding an additional websocket sub-protocol? I like the control frame approach but prefer reusing existing framing if possible.
Ava Martinez: Responding, we intentionally keep framing as a lightweight JSON control envelope to avoid incompatibilities with SSE parsers; it's feature-flagged and ignored by older clients.
Priya Desai: The default 5s pause window seems arbitrary; can we make it configurable via tenant config?
Ava Martinez: Yes, added tenant-level rollout.feature.schema_handshake.pause_window_seconds with default 5; documented.
Marco Ruiz: Suggest adding more graceful fallback telemetry so SRE can distinguish client-triggered pauses from model stalls.
Ava Martinez: Added observability events and an alert that surfaces pause/resume counts per tenant. Also included a debug_hint field in all error frames.
ci_log: All checks passed: unit tests 312/312, integration tests 48/48, lint OK, go vet clean, python style OK. One flaky SSE test retried and passed.
release_notes: Introduce optional streaming handshake and human-friendly schema error codes. Clients can opt-in to pause/resume streaming to allow client-side reconciliation of partial structured outputs. Adds OpenAI-compat verification frame for function_call responses. Backwards compatible by default.
post_merge_actions: Enable rollout.feature.schema_handshake for internal beta. Monitor schema-error-rate and pause-resume metrics. Publish docs and SDK snippets. Follow-up: telemetry dashboard to show top schema_hint values.
extra_context: This PR was driven by several customer support tickets where integrations failed silently due to malformed streamed JSON. The control frame design aims to be minimal and interoperable with SSE/WebSocket clients; we intentionally avoided binary framing to keep compatibility with serverless edge endpoints.
notes_for_backport: Not required for patch branches. If backporting to release/*, disable feature flag by default to avoid unexpected behavior.
human_readable_summary: Adds client-facing schema error codes and a short-lived pause/resume handshake for streaming structured outputs to make stream failures debuggable and reduce support noise. Includes OpenAI-compatible verification for function_call outputs.
